html:
The First Barbary War was fought from 1801 to 1805 between the United States and Tripoli, whose ruler, Yusuf of the Karamanli dynasty, declared war when the Americans refused to pay more tribute for safe passage.

President Thomas Jefferson sent the navy. In 1803 the frigate Philadelphia ran aground off Tripoli and was captured with its crew; a raiding party burned it in the harbour the next year. In 1805 a small force of US Marines and hired soldiers marched across the desert from Egypt and took Derna.

A peace followed, with a ransom for the prisoners. The war was the first fought by the United States overseas, and the Marines' hymn still recalls "the shores of Tripoli". See also the Barbary slave trade.
